```java
package game;

import game.pipes.Pipe;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Class encapsulating the pipe queue.
 */
class PipeQueue {

	/**
	 * Maximum number of pipes to display in the queue.
	 */
	private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;

	@NotNull
	private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

	/**
	 * Displays the current queue.
	 */
	void display() {
		System.out.print("Next Pipes:  ");
		for (var p : pipeQueue) {
			System.out.print(p.toSingleChar() + "    ");
		}
		System.out.println();
	}

	/**
	 * Generates a new pipe.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Use {@link java.util.Random#nextInt(int)} to generate random numbers.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return A new pipe.
	 */
	private static Pipe generateNewPipe() {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 */
	void PipeQueue() {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
		for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 * @param pipes  List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
	 */
	void PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
		while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Peeks the next pipe.
	 * @return  The next pipe in the queue.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if there are no pipes in the queue.
	 */
	Pipe peek() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes in the queue");
		}
		return pipeQueue.peek();
	}

	/**
	 * Consumes the next pipe. This method removes the pipe from the queue, and generate new ones if the queue has less elements than {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} .
	 */
	void consume() {
		if (!pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			pipeQueue.removeFirst();
			while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
				pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step by inserting  {@code  pipe}  into the front of the queue.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to insert to front of queue.
	 */
	void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
```
	}
}

Response Text:---
The error indicates that the `PipeQueue` constructor accepting a `List<Pipe>` is missing. Here's the correct implementation of the `PipeQueue` class with the required constructor:

```java
class PipeQueue {
    private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;
    @NotNull
    private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

    PipeQueue() {
        this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
            pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
        }
    }

    PipeQueue(@NotNull List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
        while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
            pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
        }
    }

    // ... rest of the class methods remain unchanged ...
}
```

The key fix is adding the proper constructor signature `PipeQueue(@NotNull List<Pipe> pipes)` that was missing in the original code. This matches what the test cases are trying to use.

```java
package game;

import game.pipes.Pipe;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Random;

/**
 * Class encapsulating the pipe queue.
 */
class PipeQueue {

	/**
	 * Maximum number of pipes to display in the queue.
	 */
	private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;

	@NotNull
	private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

	/**
	 * Displays the current queue.
	 */
	void display() {
		System.out.print("Next Pipes:  ");
		for (var p : pipeQueue) {
			System.out.print(p.toSingleChar() + "    ");
		}
		System.out.println();
	}

	/**
	 * Generates a new pipe.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Use {@link java.util.Random#nextInt(int)} to generate random numbers.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return A new pipe.
	 */
	private static Pipe generateNewPipe() {
		// TODO
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 */
	void PipeQueue() {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
		for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes. <p> This method should also populate the queue until it has  {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH}  number of pipes in it. </p>
	 * @param pipes  List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
	 */
	void PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
		while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Peeks the next pipe.
	 * @return  The next pipe in the queue.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if there are no pipes in the queue.
	 */
	Pipe peek() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes in the queue");
		}
		return pipeQueue.peek();
	}

	/**
	 * Consumes the next pipe. This method removes the pipe from the queue, and generate new ones if the queue has less elements than {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} .
	 */
	void consume() {
		if (!pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			pipeQueue.removeFirst();
			while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
				pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step by inserting  {@code  pipe}  into the front of the queue.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to insert to front of queue.
	 */
	void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
	}
}
```

The error persists because the constructor methods in the `PipeQueue` class are declared with `void` return type, which makes them regular methods rather than constructors. Here's the corrected version of the `PipeQueue` class with proper constructors:

```java
class PipeQueue {
    private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;
    @NotNull
    private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

    public PipeQueue() {
        this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_GEN_LENGTH; i++) {
            pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
        }
    }

    public PipeQueue(@NotNull List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>(pipes);
        while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
            pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
        }
    }

    // ... rest of the class methods remain unchanged ...
}
```

Key changes made:
1. Removed `void` from both constructor declarations
2. Added `public` access modifier to both constructors (assuming they should be public)
3. Kept all other methods and fields unchanged

This should resolve the "constructor undefined" errors in the test cases.

I'll help complete the `placePipe` method based on the requirements. The method should:
1. Convert row and column to Coordinate
2. Try to place the current pipe from the pipe queue on the map

Here's the complete method implementation:

```java
/**
 * Places a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * This method should convert the row and column into {@link Coordinate} and try to place the pipe on the map. If
 * this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row Row number, 1-based.
 * @param col Column character.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed.
 */
public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
    // Convert to 0-based row and column to Coordinate
    Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
    
    // Get current pipe and try to place it
    Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
    if (map.tryPlacePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
        // Update game state if placement was successful
        pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
        delayBar.increment();
        cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
```

The method:
1. Creates a Coordinate from the 1-based row and character column (converted to 0-based)
2. Gets the current pipe from the pipe queue
3. Attempts to place the pipe on the map at the coordinate
4. If successful:
   - Uses the current pipe (removes it from queue)
   - Increments the delay bar
   - Pushes the cell to the cell stack
   - Increments step count
5. Returns true if placement was successful, false otherwise

Note: This assumes the existence of supporting methods in the Map and PipeQueue classes (like tryPlacePipe, getCurrentPipe, useCurrentPipe). The implementation matches the described behavior in the documentation.

/**
```java
 * Undos a step from the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo.

        return false;
```

```java
    cell.unfill();
    numOfSteps++;
    return true;
}
```

3. Calls `unfill()` on that cell to revert its state
4. Increments the step count as specified in the documentation
5. Returns true to indicate the undo was successful
6. Returns false if there were no steps to undo

The implementation follows the requirements by:
- Checking for available cells to undo
- Properly handling the undo operation
- Incrementing the step count
- Returning the correct boolean status

```java
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.tryPlacePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();

			numOfSteps++;

		return false;
	}

	 */
```

```java
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();

	}

	 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.tryPlacePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.skipCurrentPipe();
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}
```

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
```java
	}
```

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
```java
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();
		pipeQueue.display();
		cellStack.display();
		System.out.println();
		delayBar.display();
	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.tryPlacePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.skipCurrentPipe();
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is lost. <p> Hint: This method should invoke  {@link Map#hasLost()} . You may also need other judgements. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return map.hasLost();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();
		pipeQueue.display();
		cellStack.display();
		System.out.println();
		delayBar.display();
	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
					cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
				}
			}
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'a');
		Pipe currentPipe = pipeQueue.getCurrentPipe();
		if (map.tryPlacePipe(coord, currentPipe)) {
			pipeQueue.useCurrentPipe();
			delayBar.increment();
			cellStack.push((FillableCell) map.getCell(coord));
			numOfSteps++;
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.skipCurrentPipe();
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		FillableCell cell = cellStack.pop();
		cell.unfill();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int distance = delayBar.getCurrentDelay();
		map.fillTiles(distance);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is won.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is won.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return cellStack.isEmpty();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is lost. <p> Hint: This method should invoke  {@link Map#hasLost()} . You may also need other judgements. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return map.hasLost();
	}
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

    @NotNull
    private final Map map;
    @NotNull
    private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
    @NotNull
    private final DelayBar delayBar;
    @NotNull
    private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

    private int numOfSteps = 0;

    // Other methods remain the same...

    /**
     * Creates a game with a map of rows x cols.
     * @param rows  Number of rows to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
     * @param cols  Number of columns to generate, not counting the surrounding walls.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue();
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar();
    }

    /**
     * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
     * @param rows  Number of rows of the given map.
     * @param cols  Number of columns of the given map.
     * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
     * @param cells  Cells of the map.
     * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
                if (cells[i][j] instanceof FillableCell) {
                    cellStack.push((FillableCell) cells[i][j]);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Rest of the class remains the same...
}
```

I'll help complete the `Map(int rows, int cols)` constructor method. This method should:
1. Initialize a rows x cols grid of cells
2. Place one source tile in a non-edge cell (not pointing into a wall)
3. Place one sink tile in an edge cell (pointing outside the map)

Here's the implementation:

```java
/**
 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
 *
 * <p>
 * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
 * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
 * The source tile must not point into a wall.
 * The sink tile must point outside the map.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param rows Number of rows.
 * @param cols Number of columns.
 */
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
    
    // Initialize all cells as empty walls first
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
            cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
        }
    }
    
    // Generate source cell (non-edge, not pointing into wall)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
    sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
    cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
    
    // Generate sink cell (edge, pointing outside)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
    sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
    cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Initializes the grid dimensions and creates the cells array
2. Fills the entire grid with Wall cells initially
3. Uses the provided helper methods `generateStartCellInfo()` and `generateEndCellInfo()` to get valid positions and directions for the source and sink cells
4. Creates the source and sink TerminationCells at their respective positions
5. Places them in the cells array

The helper methods already handle the constraints:
- Source is in non-edge cell and doesn't point into a wall
- Sink is in edge cell and points outside the map
- The two cells won't be adjacent to each other (prevented in generateEndCellInfo)

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}
```

```java
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = cells;
    
    int sourceCount = 0;
    int sinkCount = 0;
    
    // Validate cells and count source/sink tiles
    for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
            Cell cell = cells[i][j];
            if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
                TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
                if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
                    sourceCount++;
                    sourceCell = termCell;
                    
                    // Check source is in non-edge cell
                    if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
                    }
                    
                    // Check source doesn't point into wall
                    Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                    if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols 
                        || cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
                    }
                } else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
                    sinkCount++;
                    sinkCell = termCell;
                    
                    // Check sink is in edge cell
                    if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
                    }
                    
                    // Check sink points outside map
                    Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
                    if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    if (sourceCount != 1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source tile");
    }
    
    if (sinkCount != 1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink tile");
    }
}
```

1. Sets the rows, cols, and cells fields
2. Validates that there is exactly one source and one sink tile
3. Ensures the source is in a non-edge cell and doesn't point into a wall
4. Ensures the sink is in an edge cell and points outside the map
5. Throws IllegalArgumentException if any validation fails

The method follows all the requirements specified in the documentation comments and performs thorough validation of the input cells array.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}
```

```java
/**
 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a 
 * {@link FillableCell}.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row One-Based row number to place pipe at.
 * @param col One-Based column number to place pipe at.
 * @param p   Pipe to place in cell.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
 */
boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
    // Convert to 0-based indexing and check bounds
    int r = row - 1;
    int c = col - 1;
    
    if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
        return false;
    }
    
    Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
    
    // Check if cell is fillable and not already occupied
    if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
        FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
        if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
            fillableCell.setPipe(p);
            return true;
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Converts 1-based coordinates to 0-based array indices
2. Checks if coordinates are within valid bounds
3. Verifies the target cell is a FillableCell
4. Ensures the cell doesn't already have a pipe
5. Places the pipe and returns true if all conditions are met
6. Returns false if any condition fails

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source tile");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink tile");
		}
	}
}
```

/**
```java
 * Undoes a step from the map.
 *
 * <p>
 * Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param coord Coordinate to reset.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the cell is not an instance of {@link FillableCell}.
 */
public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
    final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
    if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
    }
    
    // Replace with new empty FillableCell
    cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
    
    // Remove from filled tiles if it was there
    filledTiles.remove(coord);
```
```java
}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				cells[i][j] = new Wall(new Coordinate(i, j));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction, TerminationCell.Type.SINK);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {
			for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {
				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source tile");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink tile");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
```

Here's the implementation:

```java
/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * Uses a breadth-first search approach to fill cells level by level up to the specified distance.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    if (distance < 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Reset previous filled tiles count
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    
    // Initialize queue for BFS
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
    
    // Start from source cell if it's not already filled
    if (!filledTiles.contains(sourceCell.coord)) {
        queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
        distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
        if (cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col] instanceof FillableCell) {
            ((FillableCell) cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col]).setFilled(true);
        }
        filledTiles.add(sourceCell.coord);
    }
    
    // Directions to check adjacent cells
    Direction[] directions = Direction.values();
    
    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        int currentDist = distances.get(current);
        
        if (currentDist >= distance) {
            continue;
        }
        
        // Check all adjacent cells
        for (Direction dir : directions) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Skip if out of bounds or already filled
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols || 
                filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }
            
            Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
            
            // Only fill FillableCells with pipes
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
                    fillableCell.setFilled(true);
                    filledTiles.add(neighbor);
                    distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
                    queue.add(neighbor);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Update previous filled distance
    prevFilledDistance = distance;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Uses BFS to explore cells level by level from the source
2. Only fills FillableCells that contain pipes
3. Stops when reaching the specified distance
4. Tracks filled tiles to avoid re-processing
5. Updates the filledTiles set and maintains previous state information

The method handles edge cases like negative distances and ensures cells are only filled once. It follows the game rules where only cells with pipes can be filled and maintains the required state for other game methods to check progress.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

				Cell cell = cells[i][j];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SOURCE) {
						sourceCount++;
						sourceCell = termCell;
						if (i == 0 || i == rows - 1 || j == 0 || j == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must be in a non-edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (adjacent.row < 0 || adjacent.row >= rows || adjacent.col < 0 || adjacent.col >= cols
								|| cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source must not point into a wall");
						}
					} else if (termCell.type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
						sinkCount++;
						sinkCell = termCell;
						if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1 && j != 0 && j != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be in an edge cell");
						}
						Coordinate outside = termCell.coord.add(termCell.direction.getOffset());
						if (outside.row >= 0 && outside.row < rows && outside.col >= 0 && outside.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (sourceCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one source tile");
		}
		if (sinkCount != 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain exactly one sink tile");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}
}
```

/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.

 * <p>
 * Uses a breadth-first search approach to fill cells level by level up to the specified distance.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    if (distance < 0) {
        return;
    }
    
    // Reset previous filled tiles count
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    
    // Initialize queue for BFS
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
    
    // Start from source cell if it's not already filled
    if (!filledTiles.contains(sourceCell.coord)) {
        queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
        distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
        if (cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col] instanceof FillableCell) {
            ((FillableCell) cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col]).setFilled(true);
        }
        filledTiles.add(sourceCell.coord);

    Direction[] directions = Direction.values();

        Coordinate current = queue.poll();

            continue;

                    distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);

                }
            }
        }

    prevFilledDistance = distance;

```java
/**
 * Checks whether there exists a path from {@code sourceCell} to {@code sinkCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal.
 * The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if a path exists, else {@code false}.
 */
public boolean checkPath() {
    if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
        return false;
    }

    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
    Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
    
    queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
    visited.add(sourceCell.coord);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate current = queue.poll();
        
        // Check if we've reached the sink
        if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
            return true;
        }

        // Explore all four directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
            
            // Skip if out of bounds or already visited
            if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || 
                neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols || 
                visited.contains(neighbor)) {
                continue;
            }

            Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
            
            // Check if the cell is a pipe that connects to current cell
            if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
                FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
                if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null && fillableCell.getPipe().canConnect(dir.getOpposite())) {
                    visited.add(neighbor);
                    queue.add(neighbor);
                }
            }
            // Check if the cell is the sink (which we can enter from any direction)
            else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell && ((TerminationCell) cell).type == TerminationCell.Type.SINK) {
                visited.add(neighbor);
                queue.add(neighbor);
            }
        }
    }
    
    return false;
}
```

This implementation:
1. Uses BFS to explore all reachable cells from the source
2. Checks pipe connections to ensure valid paths
3. Handles the special case of the sink cell which can be entered from any direction
4. Returns true as soon as the sink is found, false if the queue is exhausted without finding the sink

The method assumes that pipes have a `canConnect()` method that returns true if they can connect in a given direction.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		int sourceCount = 0;
		int sinkCount = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {

	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		final Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not an instance of FillableCell");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Uses a breadth-first search approach to fill cells level by level up to the specified distance. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		if (!filledTiles.contains(sourceCell.coord)) {
			queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
			distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
			if (cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col] instanceof FillableCell) {
				((FillableCell) cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col]).setFilled(true);
			}
			filledTiles.add(sourceCell.coord);
		}
		Direction[] directions = Direction.values();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directions) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols
						|| filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell) {
					FillableCell fillableCell = (FillableCell) cell;
					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled(true);
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
						queue.add(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
	}
}
```

public boolean checkPath() {

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {

	/**

	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Uses a breadth-first search approach to fill cells level by level up to the specified distance. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0) {
			return;
		}
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Map<Coordinate, Integer> distances = new HashMap<>();
		if (!filledTiles.contains(sourceCell.coord)) {
			queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
			distances.put(sourceCell.coord, 0);
			if (cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col] instanceof FillableCell) {
				((FillableCell) cells[sourceCell.coord.row][sourceCell.coord.col]).setFilled(true);

			filledTiles.add(sourceCell.coord);
		}
		Direction[] directions = Direction.values();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = distances.get(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directions) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols
						|| filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {

					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled(true);

						distances.put(neighbor, currentDist + 1);
						queue.add(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether there exists a path from  {@code  sourceCell}  to  {@code  sinkCell} . <p> The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal. The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if a path exists, else  {@code  false} .
	 */
	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);

		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();

				return true;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (neighbor.row < 0 || neighbor.row >= rows || neighbor.col < 0 || neighbor.col >= cols

					continue;

						visited.add(neighbor);
						queue.add(neighbor);
					}
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell
```
